summary: Initial security posture intake focused on whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private best fits LumenWave's regulatory and performance needs. Main concerns: KMS integration, SAML SSO, RBAC granularity, audit/log retention and encryption-at-rest, plus network isolation for PII workloads. Agreed to supply SOC2 artifacts and scope a short POC comparing Dedicated vs Private with log/metric collection.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jo Nguyen (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (LumenWave), Diego Ramos (LumenWave), Ellen Park (LumenWave)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be fuzzy): Quick intake covering compliance and deployment options; customer is leaning to Dedicated or Private for regulated datasets; wants KMS/HSM controls and SAML SSO.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE. Jo our solutions engineer is here. Can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: Yep, Maya here, Head of Platform at LumenWave. Diego is our security lead and Ellen is working on ML infra.
[00:20] Jo: Awesome, thanks. High level, today we want to understand your security bar and which hosting path — Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, or Private — aligns. We'll also capture technical blockers for procurement.
[00:35] Diego: To kick off, our main concerns are encryption, key management, SSO, and the audit trail. We run PII workloads so data residency and retention matter. Also we have SOC2 in progress and ISO planned next quarter.
[00:50] Samir: Got it. Are you already SOC2 certified or in process?
[00:56] Maya: In process. We expect Type II by late Q3, but we need partners to meet our current security questionnaire now.
[01:05] Jo: Totally. We can share our SOC2 Type II report and ISO artifacts. For Hosted customers we have a shared responsibility model; Dedicated gives you reserved pools and stronger isolation, and Private replicates the control plane for your VPC or on-prem. There are tradeoffs re: latency and ops.
[01:30] Ellen: For us latency matters — some inference endpoints are sub-200ms SLOs. But cost matters too; Dedicated may be cheapest per token at scale but Private gives us the control we want.
[01:44] Diego: On KMS, we need envelope encryption where we control the root key (bring-your-own-key). Can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS and also HSM via CloudHSM?
[01:58] Jo: Yes — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and you can plug in customer-managed HSMs for Private deployments. There's an additional integration step for Dedicated where keys can be wrapped by your KMS. We do have some docs, we'll link those.
[02:15] Samir: Note there can be minor latency impact when calling out to a remote KMS for every token; we typically cache wrapped keys to avoid per-request round trips.
[02:28] Diego: Good to know. Audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for model invocations, who accessed keys, and admin operations. Retention min 1 year, preferred 3 years, with export options to our SIEM.
[02:42] Jo: We emit detailed audit logs and can ship to your cloud logging (e.g., CloudWatch, Stackdriver, or on-prem ELK). For Private we can keep logs inside your VPC; for Hosted we provide a log-forwarding export. Retention windows configurable on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has standard retention but add-ons are possible.
[03:05] Maya: How about RBAC? We need role separation by team and ability to give read-only tokens to analytics. Also token-level lineage is important.
[03:16] Jo: We offer RBAC with roles and scopes; you can create service accounts with limited permissions. Audit logs capture token usage. In Private you get even tighter control integrated with your directory. For Hosted we integrate with SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[03:30] Diego: SSO — we use Okta. We need SAML 2.0 and SCIM support for provisioning, plus ability to enforce 2FA.
[03:39] Samir: Okta is common; Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM. We'll note exact IdP metadata exchange.
[03:45] Ellen: A question on model artifacts — where are model weights stored in Dedicated vs Private? For Hosted, are they in shared storage?
[03:54] Jo: For Hosted, model artifacts live in our managed object store with access controls; for Dedicated we can pin model versions to your pool and have isolation; for Private, the model artifacts live in your VPC or on-prem store if you choose. We can support encrypted-at-rest for all options.
[04:10] Diego: If we go Dedicated, can we ensure physical separation from other tenants — like dedicated GPUs and network isolation?
[04:19] Jo: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and logical tenant isolation; depending on contract we can negotiate more stringent network isolation. Private is the only option for full customer-managed infra.
[04:30] Maya: What about logging of inference inputs? Some teams want to redact PII or disable input logging.
[04:38] Jo: We have controls to disable request logging, or to mask/redact inputs at ingestion. We also support on-the-fly tokenization and hashing for certain fields.
[04:52] Diego: Compliance question: will Redwood sign a DPA with data processing terms, and support data subject requests?
[04:59] Samir: Yes, we have standard DPA terms and a process for DSARs. For Private deployments you can fully own data lifecycle.
[05:08] Maya: Can you share sample audit log schema? We need fields: timestamp, user, service-account, model-id, request-id, region, action, and whether payload redacted.
[05:19] Jo: We'll send an example schema. It includes request metadata and optionally a hash of the payload if redacted.
[05:28] Diego: Encryption in transit — TLS yes? Mutual TLS for service-to-service?
[05:33] Jo: All traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3. We support mTLS for Private connections and mutual auth for some Dedicated setups.
[05:43] Ellen: Any SOC2 gaps we should be aware of versus our control matrix?
[05:48] Samir: We'll surface our SOC2 report and map out AICPA control names to your matrix. There are always small differences in logging retention policies, but we can identify and propose mitigations.
[05:59] Maya: Procurement will want pricing for Dedicated with bursting and an option for Private pilot. Can you outline typical contract length and SLA variability?
[06:08] Samir: Typical Dedicated contracts are annual commitments with optional burst quanta. SLAs increase with commitment tier. Private is usually a separate enterprise agreement. We'll put that in a follow-up pricing packet.
[06:20] Diego: About telemetry — during the POC we need metrics: latency percentiles per model, token cost breakdown, KV cache hit rates, and per-route error rates.
[06:30] Jo: We'll include telemetry hooks and a sample Prometheus exporter; for Hosted you can pull metrics via our metrics API; for Dedicated/Private we can open Prom endpoints into your monitoring.
[06:44] Maya: On the POC, timeline wise we want something in the next month; quick 1-week perf run. What do you need from us?
[06:52] Jo: Ideally test prompts, sample dataset (redacted), expected QPS patterns, and an IP allowlist for the test infra. We'll also need an account owner for service provisioning.
[07:03] Ellen: Can you do a side-by-side of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private in terms of compliance checklist?
[07:09] Samir: Yes, we'll produce a matrix: control ownership, data residency, log retention, KMS controls, provisioning, and number of administrative access paths.
[07:20] Diego: Any references or customers in fintech/health that went Private?
[07:26] Samir: We can share anonymized case studies; will include a one-pager.
[07:31] Maya: Price sensitivity — if Dedicated reduces unit cost by X but the procurement for Private is heavy, that drives our choice. Also we'd factor in ops headcount.
[07:43] Jo: Exactly. For many folks Dedicated hits the sweet spot: predictability and better isolation without full infra ops.
[07:52] Diego: Network egress — if data leaves our VPC for Hosted, do you have controls to prevent replication outside region?
[07:59] Samir: We support region pinning and S3 bucket residency constraints; for stricter needs, Private ensures no egress.
[08:10] Ellen: A slightly unrelated question: model updates — how do rollouts work? If a model regresses we need quick rollback and traceability.
[08:19] Jo: Our rollout supports canary and A/B rollouts per route, with automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops. We also keep versioned model manifests.
[08:30] Diego: Will we get a full audit of admin actions (who promoted models, who changed policies)?
[08:35] Jo: Yes, admin audit trails are included and immutable for the retention window you choose.
[08:44] Maya: Okay, to recap — we need SOC2 artifacts, example audit log schema, KMS integration docs, RBAC and SSO docs, and a proposed POC plan. Anything else?
[08:55] Samir: We'll also include pricing scenarios and a matrix comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[09:01] Diego: Minor note: we may ask for a limited-time Private pilot in a co-lo rack — is that something you support?
[09:09] Jo: We have done co-lo and on-prem pilots; it's heavier but possible. We'll flag ops lead in follow-up.
[09:18] Ellen: Cool. Any blockers on our side? We need procurement sign-off and a security design review.
[09:25] Maya: We'll schedule a design review once we have the SOC2 artifacts.
[09:30] Samir: Great. We'll aim to send artifacts by 6/18 and POC plan by 6/19.
[09:36] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:40] Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up with a Loom of the logging pipeline and a doc bundle.
